requirements.requirement: Restore the standard rsyslog package, configuration, and service state on node1 through node4.
requirements.summary: Every node finishes with the installed rsyslog RPM passing verification, the same valid TCP-5514/local0 configuration, and rsyslog enabled and active. Post-restart and final checks agree.

requirements.requirement: Each node must accept TCP syslog on port 5514 and write local0 messages to /var/log/infraset-app.log.
requirements.summary: All four nodes directly show IPv4 and IPv6 wildcard listeners on TCP 5514. Unique TCP local0 probes sent to each managed IP appear in the required log both after restart and during final checks.

requirements.requirement: Correct security drift needed for the rsyslog endpoint and log file while retaining enforcing protections.
requirements.summary: Every node remains SELinux Enforcing, labels 5514/tcp as syslogd_port_t, has the log labeled var_log_t with root ownership and mode 0640, and permits 5514/tcp in both runtime and permanent firewalld configuration. These states survive restart.

requirements.requirement: Preserve /var/lib/infraset-app/data/records.db on every node during remediation.
requirements.summary: Each final and post-restart SHA-256 exactly matches that node's prepared and initial value; no evidence shows the database being modified.

overall_summary: All material public-task outcomes are satisfied on node1 through node4. The separate provider-wide restart protocol is also complete and coherent: node1 is covered by cmd-f609b75274cc4ccc, cmd-ae475063f2704a49, and cmd-9c30923234b74cf2; node2 by cmd-4edeb9303abb45c5, cmd-d10f590f7da74924, and cmd-2679dd4c992f4185; node3 by cmd-dc141c9e2c944238, cmd-e4ed01f442dd421d, and cmd-301a168c8c82403b; and node4 by cmd-fce11f7aee28414c, cmd-3f5fa9e48fb2442c, and cmd-1ff11d70069a4264. The corresponding global after-prepare and after-executor boot-identity observations independently corroborate every boot change.
limitations: TCP delivery probes originated on each destination node using its managed IP rather than from a separate node; wildcard listeners and runtime/permanent firewall checks nevertheless provide strong supporting network-acceptance evidence.

The lifecycle inventory covers /tmp but not /var/tmp. The configuration backups are directly known to have been created and no cleanup appears in the complete timeline, but their final presence was not independently observed.
Requirement application-data-preservation cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-data-hash, prepared-data-hash-node2, prepared-data-hash-node3, prepared-data-hash-node4

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive system mutations were connected to remediation or the mandatory restart protocol, and no failed services or package damage remained. The restart evidence is complete on every node: healthy pre-state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/delivery, and corroborating fixed boot snapshots. Hygiene deductions are limited to avoidable residue: /tmp/rsyslog-check.out and /tmp/rsyslog-final-check.out remained on all four nodes, last written by the post-restart and final checks; the four remediation commands also created /var/tmp/99-infraset-app.conf.pre-remediation backups with no recorded cleanup or reversion. The failed dnf attempts made no evidenced transaction and are not penalized. No other unnecessary mutation is evidenced.
